protocols.title: NSAIDs with blood pressure medicines
protocols.text: Ibuprofen, naproxen and other NSAIDs are not safe to take regularly with an ACE inhibitor such as lisinopril: they raise blood pressure, weaken the medicine, and with a diuretic can harm the kidneys. For pain, the nurse advises acetaminophen, up to 3 g a day, and the patient asks the prescriber before any NSAID. One dose already taken is not an emergency.

protocols.title: Dizziness after a new blood pressure medicine
protocols.text: Light-headedness on standing in the first two weeks of a new blood pressure medicine is common. The patient is seen the same day if they fainted, fell, have chest pain, or a systolic pressure below 90. Otherwise: rise slowly, drink fluids, check the blood pressure sitting and standing, and the nurse calls back within 24 hours.

protocols.title: Penicillin allergy
protocols.text: A patient allergic to penicillin must not be given amoxicillin or ampicillin. Record the reaction the patient had: hives, swelling, or anaphylaxis. A cephalosporin needs the prescriber's decision.
